# Finite support roofs, an exact sampled-facet partition, and lower-rank loads

The finite ambient-facet cover proposed by the contributor is valid, including at
sampled boundary bases. It has a useful stronger version: a finite affine
tie perturbation partitions the sampled facet mass into lattice-complete
pieces without overcounting. On each piece the selected cap's section
selector gives a genuine lower-integer-rank lift, and the other menu caps'
proper traces are retained exactly. The complementary layer remains a
real geometric obstruction to promoting that lift alone to a payment.

Work relative to the affine hull of the complete finite base P, identifying
its induced lattice with Z^n. Replace the ambient body by the canonical
convex hull C of its sampled fibers; this preserves every actual sampled
fiber. Assume those fibers are positive d-dimensional. Intrinsic reductions
can be made separately if needed.

## 1. The finite concave support roof and every boundary base

Fix a nonzero continuous normal n and put h_z=h_(K_z)(n). Define on
Q=conv(P)

    g(t)=max{sum_z lambda_z h_z:
                 lambda>=0, sum lambda=1, sum lambda z=t}.       (1)

The feasible coefficient polytope is compact. Convex compatibility gives
g(z)<=h_z at every sampled integer z, while the single coefficient at z
gives the reverse inequality. Hence g(z)=h_z. More generally g(t) is the
actual support height in direction n of the canonical real fiber C_t:
support-maximizing points from the finitely many K_z attain each feasible
weighted height in (1), and the converse follows from the canonical hull.

The hypograph of g is the convex hull of the finitely many points (z,h_z)
plus the downward vertical ray, restricted to Q. It is a polyhedron. Thus
there is a finite list of affine majorants ell_1,...,ell_m with

    g(t)=min_j ell_j(t) on Q,                         (2)

and each retained contact cell Q_j={g=ell_j} has full base dimension n.
If all lifted data are coplanar, one affine function suffices. Otherwise
take the nonvertical upper facets of the finite lifted polytope/hypograph.
Redundant pieces or lower-dimensional domains can be omitted.

The CLOSED full-dimensional contact cells cover ALL of Q, including its
relative boundary. For example approach any boundary point through the
relative interior, select a fixed active piece on a subsequence, and use
continuity of this finite polyhedral roof. Equivalently this follows
directly from the finite minimum representation (2). There is no loss of
sampled boundary bases.

For every piece, the plane n.x=ell_j(z) supports C globally. Its face

    F_j=C intersect {n.x=ell_j(z)}

projects exactly onto Q_j. If at ANY sampled z in Q_j the own supporting
patch K_z intersect {n.x=h_z} has positive (d-1)-area, F_j is an actual
ambient facet: the patch supplies d-1 independent vertical directions,
and its full-rank projection supplies n independent directions modulo
those. Its dimension is n+d-1. This argument works even when that sampled
z is on the boundary of Q_j or Q. When d=1, use zero-dimensional area1
and the same dimension count.

Every positive-area sampled supporting patch therefore lies in at least
one ACTUAL ambient facet from this finite list. Repeating for the finite
list of outer continuous normals occurring among selected caps gives a
finite cover of all their positive-area supporting patches. Arbitrary
curvature of the other parts of the fibers causes no difficulty.

## 2. A finite perturbation removes sampled-facet overcounting

The closed roof cells may overlap at integer bases. Such overlaps cannot
be discarded as ambient-surface null: their own-fiber facets can have
positive (d-1)-area. Instead choose distinct finite numbers b_j and a
sufficiently small epsilon>0, and compare the affine functions

    ell_j(t)+epsilon b_j.

Because P and the affine list are finite, epsilon can be chosen so that
at every z in P the unique perturbed minimum is one of its original
minimizers. Explicitly, take epsilon times max|b_i-b_j| smaller than the
smallest positive difference |ell_i(z)-ell_j(z)| appearing on P. Original
ties are then resolved by the distinct b_j, and nonzero gaps cannot close.

Let A_j be the closed polyhedral comparison cell where this perturbed
piece is minimal, and put P_j=P intersect A_j. The P_j partition P: no
sampled point lies on a tie boundary. Moreover

    conv(P_j) subset Q_j,
    conv(P_j) intersect Z^n=P_j.                      (3)

The first follows because ell_j was an ORIGINAL minimum at every point
of P_j, and every original affine comparison is preserved under convex
combination. For the second, an integer point in conv(P_j) belongs to P
by completeness and to A_j by convexity, so it belongs to P_j.

Assign the ENTIRE n-normal own facet at z to its unique index j. Equation
(3) ensures that each assigned collection is an actual compatible convex
facet family: take the canonical hull of its full facet traces. It has no
new integer bases, and its trace at each retained base is unchanged by
the original convex compatibility. Missing or degenerate facet traces
are handled as their actual sets, never replaced by arbitrary zero traces.

This produces an EXACT partition of sampled n-facet area into finite
lattice-complete pieces. Use the SAME partition for every menu cap on
this outer normal. Different outer normals have only zero own-facet-area
intersections (or distinct endpoints for d=1). Curved/non-supporting
boundary parts are retained separately; they are not discarded.

The partition is a bookkeeping/compatible-family construction, not an
assertion that each piece is separately isolatable by a physical field.
The number of pieces and the sum of their individual parity quotas need
not be bounded by one global quota.

## 3. Actual source geometry forces lower base rank on each incidence piece

Let an actual source cap have N=(a,u), source Y=(p,y), threshold
c=N.Y-b, with b=0 in the pure-width setting (or a sufficiently small
nonnegative H buffer). On a supporting facet with continuous outer normal
n, write u=s alpha n with alpha>0 and s=+-1. Its restriction to F_j is

    N.(z,x)-c=lambda_j(z)
      :=a.(z-p)+s alpha[ell_j(z)-n.y]+b.               (4)

At the actual source base,

    lambda_j(p)=s alpha[ell_j(p)-n.y]+b.

The global majorant obeys ell_j(p)>=h_p(n), while the own source inball
gives h_p(n)-n.y>=r_s|n|. Thus this value is strictly positive when s=+1
and strictly negative when s=-1 and b<alpha r_s|n|. It is never zero.
Every supporting sampled incidence of this cap in the assigned piece has
lambda_j(z)=0. Its affine base span therefore has rank at most n-1.

This remains true when p is outside Q_j: ell_j is a GLOBAL affine
majorant, and (4) uses its legitimate extrapolation, not a claim that p
belongs to that face. If P_j already has smaller rank, the reduction may
be stronger.

For a nonempty incidence set, choose one integer base p0 and take
V=span_R of its integer differences, Lambda=V intersect Z^n. This is a
full-rank lattice in rational V, regardless of irrational coefficients
in lambda_j. Include every integer base of the compact patch hull before
passing to limits. The coherent uniform-kernel selector lift then gives
an actual mixed convex body with dimensions (r,d), r<=n-1: d-1 tangent
coordinates and one added height. All anchored inclusions, including those
at sampled boundary bases, are retained as in the earlier shared-roof note.

## 4. Exact loads of the OTHER proper caps on that lift

Fix one minimal positive source circuit of continuous rank at least two.
It has no parallel or antipodal continuous normals. Thus on a given own
facet at most one selected cap j is supporting. Every other menu normal
has a nonzero tangential component there. Its limiting profile on that
facet is exactly 1_(H_k), with its zero plane having zero facet area.
This includes fully captured or empty traces as special cases.

Assigned bases where no cap of this menu supports the facet retain their
whole original regular trace separately. The following formulas concern
the supporting incidence pieces; they do not discard that other boundary.

On one assigned supporting incidence piece, write dA for the sum of
ordinary own-facet areas over its retained integer bases, tau for cap j's
coherent section selector. Let G be the GENUINE projection of its
retained convex positive-support lift, and write

    L={(z,x,t): (z,x) in G, 0<=t<=tau(z,x)}.

For a finite profile tau=clamp(g,0,1) with g concave, this uses the
nonnegative domain {g>=0}, with empty traces where g<0. Genuine
zero-height boundary traces are retained. For a limiting profile use
the actual retained convex lift and its projection; do not append
zero-height points elsewhere in the full facet. Such appended points
can destroy convexity, as tau=(1-x^2)_+ on [-2,2] demonstrates.
The vertical lengths extended by zero are tau, so its mixed d-volume
is still int tau dA. The proper trace of cap k
pulls back to the VERTICAL ambient halfspace

    Htilde_k={(z,x,t):N_k.(z,x)-c_k>=0}.

No new cap threshold or center is chosen. Exactly

    |L intersect Htilde_k|=int tau 1_(H_k) dA.         (5)

Let omega_k be the actual response weights of this source menu and let
A0=int dA, L0=|L|. For an OUTSIDE-supporting j, its own boundary capture
is tau, so the ORIGINAL weighted load equals

    omega_j L0
      +sum_(k!=j) omega_k |L intersect Htilde_k|
      +sum_(k!=j) omega_k int (1-tau)1_(H_k) dA.       (6)

For an INSIDE-supporting j, replace the first term in (6) by

    omega_j(A0-L0).                                  (7)

These are exact identities. In particular all overlaps with other caps
that cut the facet properly remain present, both on the selector layer
and on its complement. Summing (6)--(7) over the sampled-facet partition
from Section2 introduces no duplicate original boundary area. Coarea
rather than boundary area is obtained by the known constant factor
1/|u_j| on this one cap; it must be retained if changing normalization.

For a nonconstant nonnegative physical weight Phi, the same identities
hold with Phi pulled back independently of t, but the lift law is then
weighted. A uniform-volume closed-minor theorem cannot silently be applied
to that weighted law without an additional convex-lift representation.

## 5. The remaining complement and normalization obstruction

In the unit prism over the facet, the complementary layer has height
1-tau. It is generally NOT convex. Already on [-1,1] take

    tau(x)=1-x^2.

Its selector lift is convex, but the complement contains (-1,0) and(1,0)
and not their midpoint(0,0) when represented by its reflected vertical
height 1-tau. Equivalently, the full unit prism minus the actual lift
contains (-1,1/2),(1,1/2) but not (0,1/2); boundary conventions do not
affect any volume identity. This layer is essential in (6)--(7)
and in the full original area cost A0. For the proper halfspace x>=0,

    original trace area=1,
    selector-layer cap volume=2/3,
    complementary cap volume=1/3.

Thus replacing a proper trace by its cap in L loses a quantified positive
part, even for this simplest common concave roof.

Even granting a good capture fraction on L would control only the factor
L0/A0 of the original facet cost. That ratio can approach0 for genuine
concave selectors (take tau constant epsilon). The complement's costs
and cap loads therefore cannot be erased when promoting a lower-rank
minor quota to the original normalized response.

Finally, distinct assigned pieces may reuse the same residue classes.
Exact disjointness of original boundary area does not imply that their
separate constants 2^r add to at most2^n. The finite partition solves the
geometric overcounting, while parity-cost allocation, admissible physical
localization, and center/credit transfer remain separate obligations.

The genuine new interface is the non-overcounted compatible partition
(3), the actual rank reduction (4), and the full load identities (5)--(7).
No Gamma_d/2^n payment is inferred without those remaining steps.
